claim.why_it_matters: The subscripts that index the occurrences of argument-1 were flattened into the name, so the equivalent arithmetic expression for MEAN now reads as operands named argument-11 and argument-12.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of PDF page 718 (printed page 694, §2014:15.56.3 Returned values 1b) shows '((argument-1' followed by a lowered, smaller '1', then ' + argument-1' with a subscript '2', then ') / 2)'. The transcription (page-718.md line 29) reads '((argument-11 + argument-12) / 2)', with no subscript markup. Line 33 (item c) has the same defect: the PDF prints subscripts 1, 2 and n, and the markdown reads 'argument-11 + argument-12 +... + argument-1n'. Losing the subscripts is not cosmetic here. The result reads as operands named argument-11 and argument-12, which are different identifiers, instead of the first and second occurrences of argument-1. That changes the literal text of the normative equivalent expression for MEAN. A careful reader can probably recover the intent from context ('For two occurrences of argument-1'), so the risk to an implementation is low, but the transcription does misstate the content.
verdict.corrected_description: §2014:15.56.3 1b and 1c: the PDF prints argument-1 with occurrence subscripts (₁, ₂, ₙ). The markdown flattens them into the name: 'argument-11 + argument-12' in item b (line 29), and 'argument-11 + argument-12 +... + argument-1n' in item c (line 33). The claim names only item b, but item c has the same defect.
